newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU asks Russia to avoid WTO-incompatible measures.
newsitem.headline: EU asks Russia to avoid WTO-incompatible measures.

text.p: The European Commission urged Russia on Thursday to commit itself not to introduce any new measures that were incompatible with World Trade Organisation (WTO) standards, a European Commission official said..

The request was made at a meeting in Brussels between Russian Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Trade Oleg Davydov, EU Trade Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan and External Affairs Commissioner Hans van den Broek.

The official said the Commission, on behalf of the European Union, had told Davydov it was keen to see Russia in the WTO and had suggested the standstill as a way to help achieve Moscow's goal of joining.
Brittan pointed out to Davydov that China, which is also trying to join the WTO, had instituted such an agreement already, the official said.

He said Davydov replied that there was a major difference between Russia and China. China, he was reported as saying, was only interested in economic reform while Russia was seeking democratic reform as well, which complicated the idea of a standstill agreement.
Davydov said Russia was trying to develop a socially oriented market economy, the official said.

In specific sectors, the European Commission told Davydov it would like Russia to adopt an agreement by December 6 to liberalise its textile industry over four years. It would also like an agreement to liberalise the steel industry.
The official said Davydov had "bascially agreed with the objectives" but not the details, including the four-year plan.
